questions.cardText:
[Archaeology] In which country have the most pyramids been discovered?
A. Mexico
B. Sudan
C. Cambodia
Answer: B. As of 2024, Sudan has more pyramids than any other country in the world. The ancient Nubian Kingdoms of Kush built over 200 pyramids. These pyramids served as tombs for the kings and queens of Kush.
questions.de: Welches heutige Land hat mehr Pyramiden als jedes andere – errichtet als Königsgräber von den antiken nubischen Reichen von Kusch?
questions.en: Which present-day country has more pyramids than any other, built as royal tombs by the ancient Nubian kingdoms of Kush?

timeline.labelEn: Kushite kings and nobles in Nubia (today's Sudan) are buried in pyramids, c. 700 BC – AD 350
timeline.labelDe: Kuschitische Könige und Adlige in Nubien (heute Sudan) werden in Pyramiden bestattet, ca. 700 v. Chr. – 350 n. Chr.

questions.notes: Wikipedia: about 255 Nubian pyramids are known, more than double the number built in ancient Egypt (card says 'over 200').

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Other than using their breath, how do manatees control their buoyancy in the water?
A. By temporarily swallowing rocks
B. By compressing air in their stomach
C. By farting
Answer: C. Manatees can store and release gas in their intestines, allowing them to float or sink as needed. There also appears to be an association between constipation and not being able to dive, according to a reviewer of this question.
questions.de: Wie regulieren Seekühe (Manatis) ihren Auftrieb im Wasser, abgesehen von der Luft in ihrer Lunge?
questions.en: Other than with the air in their lungs, how do manatees adjust their buoyancy in the water?
questions.answerDe: Indem sie Darmgase speichern und ablassen (pupsen)
questions.answerEn: By storing and releasing intestinal gas (farting)

timeline.labelEn: Carl Linnaeus scientifically names the West Indian manatee, Trichechus manatus
timeline.labelDe: Carl Linné benennt die Karibik-Manati wissenschaftlich als Trichechus manatus

source.title: Farting fish and tooting manatees — how some animals use gas

questions.notes: Evidence is partly anecdotal: gut gas from fermenting plants is stored/compressed and released to float or sink; captive constipated manatees reportedly struggled to dive. Their dense bones (ballast) also help, per Wikipedia 'Manatee'. Timeline: species authority from Wikipedia 'West Indian manatee'.
